transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it. 

Um... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble at work. It's probably nothing major, maybe just me being tired or something, but... I'm a hairstylist, and lately, my hands just feel like they’re moving through glue. Like, even just doing the simple things, you know? Just sectioning hair or mixing color in the back... it feels like it takes me forever now. 

I really didn't want to make a big deal out of it, but some of the other girls at the salon have actually started noticing that I’m just... slower than I used to be. I really don't want anyone to think I'm slacking off or doing a bad job. Um, does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days recently?

Um... I really don't want to sound ungrateful or anything, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... yeah, I guess I have been. 

It's just... most days, I wake up with this really heavy, flat sadness right in my chest. It's hard to explain, but it almost makes me feel like there's no point in trying to build the life I was planning for myself. I always try to just push past it and put on a good face for my clients, you know? 

I hope it's okay that I'm admitting that... I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. Is it normal to feel that way?
Have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Um... I really try to stay positive, I promise I do. But, yeah, I guess things have felt a little different lately. 

I used to love chatting with all my clients and, you know, helping out the newer girls at the salon. And on my days off, I was always going hiking with my friends. But lately... I don't know, I just kind of keep my head down at work. I guess I've been avoiding people a little bit, mostly just because I don't really have that... that spark in me right now to be super social and fun. 

I feel terrible about it, because I don't want anyone to think I'm being rude or ignoring them. I'm really trying my best to be friendly, though, even when I don't feel up to it. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound antisocial or anything...
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

Oh, um... please don't be alarmed or anything, I promise I don't have any actual plan to hurt myself or do anything drastic. I really don't want you to worry about me like that. 

But... um... I guess sometimes I do get these thoughts. Just... like maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. Like, if I went to sleep and that was it, then nobody would have to deal with me or worry about me being so slow and sad anymore. 

I feel so guilty even saying that out loud, because I know it sounds terrible and I really don't want to be a burden to anyone. I would never actually do anything to hurt myself, I swear. I hope you don't think less of me for admitting that... is it okay that I told you?
Have you had any hallucinations, like hearing or seeing things that other people don’t?

Oh, um... well... I really don't want to sound crazy or anything. I know how this might sound, and I promise I'm usually very level-headed. 

But... sometimes, yeah. Like, when I'm at the salon, just sweeping up hair or rinsing out the color bowls... I'll hear this voice. It's a woman's voice, and it sounds like it's coming from right near the shampoo stations. She just... she tells me that I'm ruining everything. 

The thing is, I'll hear it even when the salon is completely empty, or when nobody is anywhere near me. I always try to ignore it and just keep working hard, because I don't want anyone to catch me looking around for someone who isn't there. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds really strange. I hope you don't think I'm losing my mind... is it okay that I shared that with you?
Do the voices only happen when you’re feeling depressed, or do they also happen when your mood feels normal?

Um... well, I really want to make sure I give you the right answer, so I've been trying to piece it together myself. 

Actually... before the sadness really took over and I started feeling so slow, there was a stretch of maybe a few weeks where my mood was fine. I was still getting up every day, functioning pretty normally, and trying my best to be a good employee. But... um... I was actually already hearing that woman's voice back then. 

And... I also felt really sure that someone at the salon was messing with my schedule on purpose. I know that probably sounds a bit paranoid, and I really do try to get along with all the girls there, I promise I'm not usually a difficult person to work with. I just... I really felt like someone was interfering with my appointments. 

I hope it's okay that I'm admitting that to you... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining about my coworkers. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information. Does that help answer your question?
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or needed much less sleep than usual?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try to make sure I get a good night's sleep so I can be on my feet all day at the salon. I'm usually pretty good about sticking to a routine, so I don't want you to think I'm out partying or staying up all night or anything like that. 

I've never really had a time where I felt super energized or didn't need to sleep. Honestly, lately it's just been the opposite with feeling so tired all the time. 

I hope that's the right answer... I just want to be completely honest with you. Is that what you were asking about?
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when the voices or the suspicious feelings continued even though you were not feeling depressed?

Um... yes, actually. I think I mentioned it just a minute ago, but... before the sadness really got bad and made me so exhausted, there was that time where my mood was actually okay. 

It was probably a few weeks, maybe even a month? I was still getting up every morning, going to the salon, and doing my best to keep my clients happy. I was functioning pretty normally, I think. But... um... that's when I first started hearing that woman's voice telling me I was ruining things. And that's also when I started feeling so sure that someone was messing with my book and moving my appointments around. 

Even though I wasn't feeling depressed yet, those things were already happening for a few weeks. I really hope I'm explaining this clearly enough for you... I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the details you need. Am I doing okay?
